channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Australian canola down but not out of China after Xi’s deal with Canada
item.description: A trade deal between China and Canada has damaged Australia’s hopes of becoming China’s main supplier of canola, but the Pacific nation’s access to the world’s biggest oilseed importer has significantly improved, traders and analysts said.

item.title: Canadian hog sector set for strong margins in 2026 says FCC
item.description: Strong demand for Canadian pork and lower feed costs seem set to support hog margins in 2026 says Farm Credit Canada.

item.title: Farm family income gains driven by off-farm earnings: Statistics Canada
item.description: Average income for families operating a single farm in Canada grew by 0.9 per cent to $216,021 in 2023 compared to 2021. However, this was driven by higher off-farm income.

item.title: United Farmers of Alberta remains stalking horse bidder for AgraCity assets
item.description: SASKATOON — An attempt to replace United Farmers of Alberta (UFA) as the stalking horse bidder for the AgraCity Group assets has failed. AgraCity is a Saskatchewan crop input provider owned by Jason Mann and James Mann. item.title: India’s strong pulse harvest may limit imports
item.description: India’s chickpea and lentil crops look good, which could minimize pea and lentil exports to that country in 2025-26.

item.title: AgCanadaTV: In case you missed it; your national ag news recap for Jan. 30, 2026
item.description: CFIA hit by federal job cuts A union representing Canadian Food Inspection Agency workers says that some 1,370 jobs will be cut at the agency. This comes after Agriculture Agri-Food Canada confirmed it was eliminating 665 positions and closing seven research centres and farms across Canada. item.title: Lower seeding rate favours mustard composite
item.description: A three-year study found composite mustard AAC Yellow 80 responds better to nitrogen than the open-pollinated Andante variety and yields higher.

item.title: Auctioneer champion returns to the big leagues
item.description: Brennin Jack, branch manager of Heartland Livestock Services in Virden, is headed to the 2026 World Livestock Auctioneering Championship.

item.title: Saskatchewan map maker helps put history on the wall
item.description: Pronghorn Maps is located in Alex McPhee’s house. There, he prints maps of all kinds — election maps, historical farm maps, Hutterite colony maps, the list goes on.

item.title: Grazing lease controversy in southern Alberta municipality reaching critical juncture
item.description: A southern Alberta rural municipality continues its years long process of balancing the needs of native grassland preservation and economic development on its tax-recovery lands.
